name: Alabama Peace Officers’ Standards and Training Commission
notes: Official commission site identifies APOSTC and its certification and officer reporting responsibilities.

name: Alaska Police Standards Council
notes: Official site identifies the council as setting and enforcing officer training, certification, ethics, and conduct standards.

name: Arizona Peace Officer Standards and Training Board
notes: Official board site identifies AZPOST and its peace officer certification process.

name: Arkansas Commission on Law Enforcement Standards and Training
notes: Selected the commission, not the Arkansas Law Enforcement Training Academy. Arkansas DPS also lists the full state-prefixed commission name at https://dps.arkansas.gov/.

name: California Commission on Peace Officer Standards and Training
notes: Official certification bureau page identifies the full commission name and POST abbreviation, certificate issuance, and certification status records.

name: Peace Officer Standards and Training Board
notes: Official Colorado POST page identifies the board and its policy and certification appeal roles; the homepage identifies Colorado Peace Officer Standards & Training (POST).

name: Police Officer Standards and Training Council
notes: Official Connecticut site explicitly states that POSTC certifies and decertifies members of Connecticut law enforcement units.

name: Police Officer Standards and Training Commission
notes: Current Delaware authority. Formerly the Council on Police Training; official site describes certification and misconduct oversight.

name: Criminal Justice Standards & Training Commission
notes: Official FDLE page identifies the commission and expressly lists officer certification, sanctions, and the State Officer Certification Examination among its responsibilities.

name: Georgia Peace Officer Standards & Training Council
notes: Official council website, distinct from the Georgia Public Safety Training Center. State certification rules also identify the council at https://rules.sos.ga.gov/gac/464-3.

name: Hawaiʻi Law Enforcement Standards Board
notes: Authority identity verified. Do not imply its certification program is already operational: official 2026 board testimony described staffing and implementation still in progress. SB2519 HD1 CD1 moves certification dates to 2028; official legislative reporting records enactment as Act 107 on June 8, 2026. Supporting sources: https://data.capitol.hawaii.gov/sessions/session2026/bills/SB2519_CD1_.PDF and https://data.capitol.hawaii.gov/advreports/advreport.aspx?measuretype=SB&report=deadline&rpt_type=passLeg_finalDecking&title=Senate+bills+that+have+passed+the+Legislature+or+been+decked+for+Final+Reading&year=2026.

name: Idaho Peace Officer Standards and Training Council
notes: Selected the council as the statutory authority. The POST division provides certification and maintains records as trustee for the council; the official page says POST derives statutory authority from the POST Council. Council name also appears in IDAPA 11.11.01.

name: Illinois Law Enforcement Training and Standards Board
notes: Official board website identifies full name and abbreviation. The state police academy confirms that officer certification is obtained from ILETSB at https://isp.illinois.gov/AcademyTraining/BasicTraining.

name: Law Enforcement Training Board
notes: Selected the governing board, not the academy. Official decertification procedure identifies the LETB hearing and revocation role: https://www.in.gov/ilea/files/Decertification-Procedures.pdf.

name: Iowa Law Enforcement Academy Council
notes: Selected the statutory council, not only the academy training facility. Iowa Code 80B.3 identifies the council; 80B.13 and 80B.13A govern its certification powers. Current official council page: https://ilea.iowa.gov/about/academy-council. No council-specific abbreviation asserted.

name: Kansas Commission on Peace Officers’ Standards and Training
notes: Official certification page identifies the commission; https://kscpost.gov/training/ provides the KSCPOST abbreviation. Distinct from the Kansas Law Enforcement Training Center.

name: Kentucky Law Enforcement Council
notes: Official council history and duties page expressly identifies certification of police officers among council functions.

name: Council on Peace Officer Standards and Training
notes: Exact council name from Louisiana's official boards directory and R.S. 40:2403. Council program page at https://lcle.la.gov/programs/post/ uses POST and describes certification. The council operates under the Louisiana Commission on Law Enforcement and Administration of Criminal Justice.

name: Maine Criminal Justice Academy Board of Trustees
notes: Selected the Board of Trustees because the official page expressly assigns it training and certification of Maine law enforcement officers. Statutory support: https://www.legis.maine.gov/statutes/25/title25sec2803-A.html. No board-specific abbreviation asserted.

name: Police Training and Standards Commission
notes: Official page expressly identifies PTSC as Maryland's police certification and training authority. Selected the police commission, not the combined administrative agency or Correctional Training Commission.

name: Massachusetts Peace Officer Standards and Training Commission
notes: Official site identifies mandatory officer certification, discipline, and training responsibilities. Selected the POST Commission, not the Municipal Police Training Committee.

name: Michigan Commission on Law Enforcement Standards
notes: Official page states that Michigan law enforcement licensing must be approved through MCOLES.

name: Board of Peace Officer Standards and Training
notes: Official Minnesota board page identifies its training and licensing rules. Minnesota Rule 6700.0200 states the board's selection, training, and licensing authority: https://www.revisor.mn.gov/rules/6700/full.

name: Board on Law Enforcement Officer Standards and Training
notes: Official Mississippi FAQ identifies BLEOST's minimum employment, training, certification, and professional conduct standards.

name: Peace Officer Standards and Training Program
notes: Selected the Missouri DPS regulatory program, which the official page explicitly says licenses peace officers and investigates license discipline. A separate POST Commission sets training standards and receives program staff support; Missouri R.S. 590.030 assigns license issuance to the DPS director.
